title: Close-area relocalization after VIO loss: scan-to-map pose hypotheses, ratio + persistence acceptance, hover until one wins
summary: Relocalizer for the close-area arena. After a detected VIO loss (reset_counter change, quality 0, or a scan-to-map innovation test) a pose source that wraps the arena's VIO-like estimator reports quality 0 (a planner gate hovers), matches the 72-beam range scan against the known 0.1 m occupancy grid by correlative grid search on a likelihood field (EDT distance, sigma 0.10 m, +-2 m window), keeps up to 5 hypotheses 0.5 m apart, and accepts one with a named rule: best score >= 0.6, best >= 1.02 x second, and the same winner for 3 scans; 'none of them' keeps hovering and widens the window to +-4 m. On accept it re-anchors the estimate. experiment.py flies the arena's A* known-map planner on 100 random layouts under the dropout and jump faults and compares no relocalization, hover only, single-hypothesis commit at once, and the multi-hypothesis rule, with ablations without the innovation test, plus a symmetric 2 m x 14.8 m corridor where shifted poses look the same. Thresholds set on seed-1 static poses (tune.py). Synthetic arena only.
verified: ran 2026-11-09 with CPython 3.12.10 + numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1 on an Apple M3 Max, in the sample venv: experiment.py --layouts 100 --seed 0 ran twice with identical tables (wall 70.7 s on 8 workers for the kept run); experiment.py --corridor --runs 20 ran once (21.3 s); tune.py on seed 1 wrote results/tune_seed1.json. Every number in README is from results/. test_smoke.py: 1 passed in the venv, 1 skipped under plain python3 without numpy. No arena file was edited. Layouts, vehicle, estimator and range sensor are simulated; yaw is truth; the map is the exact prior grid; no SITL, no real drone or lidar. Later: run_disambiguate.py --corridor --runs 20 (22 s) and --layouts 100 --seed 0 (75 s) in the sample venv (CPython 3.11.15, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1); the loop driver ran --layouts 100 --seed 1 as a held-out check (76.5 s, results/disamb_random_1.md). Acceptance thresholds came from seed-1 static poses (tune.py); no flight parameter was tuned on seed 1.
shows: What the drone does when VIO is lost indoors: scan-to-map relocalization with up to 5 hypotheses and a ratio + persistence rule vs commit-at-once vs no relocalization, under dropout and jump faults, plus a symmetric corridor
runtime: ~71 s for 100 layouts x 2 faults x 7 arms on 8 workers; corridor ~21 s; disambiguating moves ~75 s per seed, corridor ~22 s
key_result: [Disambiguating moves](README.md#disambiguating-moves-after-a-hover-timeout-loop-22b), 100 random layouts, A* known map: hover + scan-to-map hypotheses + one info-gain move after 1 s reached 99 % / 99 % (dropout / jump) on seed 0 and 100 % / 100 % on held-out seed 1, 0 wrong commits, 0 % collisions, against 64 % / 36 % with the estimator alone (1 % / 9 % collisions); commit-at-once reaches 100 % but makes 2-4 wrong commits per 100; symmetric corridor: info-gain move 80 %, hover-only rule 0 %. Synthetic, yaw is truth, exact prior map
